A huge (virtual) space telescope done cheap with cubesats?
This would work the best for radio telescopes. More specifically, when the radio source is very strong and great angular separation is needed.

Two ways to combine signals from two separate imaging devices to attain higher angular resolution: computational and optical.

For radio telescopes, computational is practical, so it's less important to have them within line of sight and aligned with great precision. One can compensate somewhat in the arithmetic. For optical telescopes, we just don't have fast enough sensors or processors to do it computationally, so they have to be kept in very precise alignment so the images can be combined optically.

Now, if you could connect them via struts, and get them far enough away from the Earth and Moon that tidal forces didn't distort the array much, it might well work.
